title: Inventors Who Changed the World
summary: Who invented what, and when: from Newton's laws to the World Wide Web.

knowledge.text: Isaac Newton lived from 1643 to 1727 and was English.
Isaac Newton published the laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation in the Principia in 1687.
Isaac Newton built the first practical reflecting telescope in 1668.
Isaac Newton co-developed calculus, which Leibniz developed independently.
James Watt lived from 1736 to 1819 and was Scottish.
James Watt improved the steam engine by adding a separate condenser patented in 1769.
James Watt's steam engine improvements made engines far more efficient and powered the Industrial Revolution.
Alexander Graham Bell lived from 1847 to 1922.
Alexander Graham Bell received the first US patent for the telephone in 1876.
Thomas Edison lived from 1847 to 1931 and was American.
Thomas Edison invented the phonograph in 1877.
Thomas Edison developed a practical, long-lasting incandescent light bulb in 1879.
Thomas Edison opened the Pearl Street Station in New York in 1882, an early direct current power station.
Nikola Tesla lived from 1856 to 1943 and was Serbian-American.
Nikola Tesla invented the AC induction motor, patented in 1888.
Nikola Tesla developed the alternating current power system, licensed to George Westinghouse.
Nikola Tesla invented the Tesla coil in 1891.
The War of the Currents took place in the late 1880s to 1890s between Edison promoting direct current and Tesla and Westinghouse promoting alternating current.
Alternating current won the War of the Currents because it can be sent long distances efficiently using transformers.
Marie Curie lived from 1867 to 1934 and was Polish-French.
Marie Curie discovered the elements polonium and radium in 1898 and pioneered research on radioactivity.
Marie Curie was the first person to win two Nobel Prizes in Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911.
The Wright brothers, Orville and Wilbur, made the first powered, controlled aeroplane flight at Kitty Hawk on 17 December 1903.
Alan Turing lived from 1912 to 1954 and was English.
Alan Turing described the Turing machine in 1936, providing the foundation of computer science.
Alan Turing helped break the German Enigma code at Bletchley Park in World War II using the Bombe machine.
J. Robert Oppenheimer lived from 1904 to 1967 and was American.
J. Robert Oppenheimer served as scientific director of the Los Alamos Laboratory in the Manhattan Project.
J. Robert Oppenheimer led the development of the first atomic bomb, tested at Trinity on 16 July 1945.
Now I am become Death, the destroyer of worlds.
Tim Berners-Lee was born in 1955 and is English.
Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

intro.text: Isaac Newton built the first practical reflecting telescope in 1668 and published laws of motion.
James Watt patented his separate condenser in 1769, powering the Industrial Revolution.
Alexander Graham Bell received the first US patent for the telephone in 1876.
Edison and Tesla clashed in the War of the Currents over direct and alternating current.
Marie Curie discovered polonium and radium in 1898 and won two Nobel Prizes.
The Wright brothers made the first powered aeroplane flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903.
